newsitem.title: INDIA: New four-nation BIST-EC group plans airline.
newsitem.headline: New four-nation BIST-EC group plans airline.

text.p: The newly formed regional grouping of Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka and Thailand Economic Cooperation named the BIST-EC, plans to launch a sub-regional airline, officials said on Monday.

"It was agreed that the first and immediate manifestation of sub-regional economic cooperation would be establishment of a sub-regional airline to be called BIST," Indian Minister of State Saleem Iqbal Shervani told a briefing.
Shervani later on Monday was appointed as a junior external affairs minister in Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's council of ministers.
BIST-EC was formally launched in Bangkok, capital of Thailand, on June 6, Shervani said.
Burma attended the BIST-EC meeting in Bangkok as an observer and is expected to shortly join the sub-regional grouping, he said.

The four member countries have pledged to hold annual ministerial meetings and senior officials would also hold regular talks on cooperation in trade, investment, industry, tourism, agriculture, energy and other development fields.
"This is consolidation of our 'Look East' policy," said A.N. Ram, a senior Indian Foreign Ministry official.
India became a full dialogue partner of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) last year.
ASEAN, grouping Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Vietnam and Thailand, is due to be joined this year by Burma, Cambodia and Laos.
